original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Prove the sharp uniform common-support29 shortening theorem for three residual pieces of binary rank at most six, with a literal common-cut30 witness; no historical caller application.
scope_change_reason: The current P112 C5 handoff and PR3255 support22 equality obligation motivate a scoped geometry theorem rather than a fully priced decoder. The same joint support/singleton audit strengthens the initial equality22 predicate to sharp29/30.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the decoder-floor C5 geometry obligation; it constrains three-endpoint code intersections. No physical child-rank budget or supplier acceptance gate is met.
stop_rule: Finish one source-bound theorem and actual next-boundary witness, obtain narrow peer check, publish and stop. No second research round.
evidence: PROOF.md, exact RESULT.json, primary complete finite premises, separate lattice/closure/witness checker, seven behavioral groups and CHECKS.json.
